## Overview

Fixes #61490. After `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)`, a request whose in-flight prefill output carried the completed prompt logprobs is resumed without re-registering the requirement on the V1 runner, so the client gets null prompt logprobs. The scheduler now marks such requests when the output is dropped as stale and passes the ids to the runner, which re-registers the requirement for the re-run prefill.

## Claims

- Fixes the null prompt logprobs from #61490 on the V1 model runner path.
- No behavior change on the default V2 runner, which already re-registers resumed requests on its new-request path, and none for requests without prompt logprobs.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`:

- `test_reset_prefix_cache_redoes_dropped_prompt_logprobs`: reset lands mid-prefill, the stale output carrying prompt logprobs is dropped, and the resumed schedule carries the redo directive exactly once (V1 runner).
- `test_stale_output_without_prompt_logprobs_sets_no_redo_flag`: a dropped stale chunk without prompt logprobs sets no marker.
- `test_redo_marker_cleared_on_v2_resume`: the V2 path clears the marker and sends no directive.

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
# 230 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on all touched files.

No GPU end-to-end run here (no CUDA build on this machine); the bug and fix live in scheduler/runner bookkeeping, which the tests above drive directly through the public scheduler API. CI covers the serving path.

## Details

Root cause: the reset preempts running requests with `drop_stale_output=True`. When the in-flight output then returns, it is discarded as stale, but that output carried the completed prompt logprobs and the runner had already retired its `num_prompt_logprobs` entry at prefill completion. The resumed request goes through the V1 cached-request path, which never re-registers the requirement, so the recomputed prefill emits no prompt logprobs.

The runner cannot infer the redo on its own: when a `num_prompt_logprobs` entry is gone it cannot distinguish "popped because delivered" from "popped because the output was dropped", and re-registering on every preemption would double-deliver for ordinary decode-time preemption. So the scheduler marks the request exactly where the stale drop happens, sends the affected ids once via `CachedRequestData.redo_prompt_logprobs_req_ids`, and the runner re-registers using the same expression as its new-request path. The marker is cleared when the directive is sent, on the V2 resumed-to-new conversion, and on any fresh schedule, so it cannot leak into a later step.

Duplicate check: no open PR references #61490, and keyword searches over open PRs (`prompt logprobs reset prefix`, `reset_prefix_cache logprobs`) turn up nothing addressing this. The issue had no linked PR and no one claimed it.

MRV1 note: this fix targets the V1 runner's cached-request path, where the bug lives. MRV2 is not affected, since it converts resumed requests into new requests and re-registers prompt logprobs there; the marker is explicitly cleared on that path.

Prepared with AI assistance (Kimi Code). I reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

nodes.body:
Hi @he-yufeng, thanks for working on this fix! I ran an independent GPU reproduction of #61490 against `20761622ac6da3fb9d2498e0aa0529c87ae796ce` and still see failures with V1 async scheduling in two fresh server runs.

The streamed echo request still raises `KeyError: 220`. The non-streamed `prompt_logprobs` request returns HTTP 500 with `OverflowError: number too small to fit in target type`; the API server then exits, interrupting the sweep.

### Environment and build scope

- Single NVIDIA RTX 4090 D, 24 GB; driver `595.71.05`.
- Python `3.12.3`; PyTorch `2.13.0` with CUDA runtime `13.0`; Triton `3.7.1`; Transformers `5.19.0`; httpx `0.28.1`.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, loaded from a local snapshot.
- Runtime: complete PR HEAD Python source, with native/vendor build artifacts and generated version metadata from the official vLLM `0.30.0` wheel. PyTorch matches the PR's CUDA requirements. All 2,662 tracked runtime Python files were checked against the HEAD source archive and were unchanged.
- Paired runtime baseline: HEAD with only the four production-file changes reversed using `patch --reverse --fuzz=0`, corresponding to merge base `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`. It used the same dependencies and precompiled artifacts.

### Results

Counts below exclude the two warmup requests in each client invocation.

| Runtime / scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Paired baseline, V1 async, no reset | 0/24 failures |
| Paired baseline, V1 async, active-request reset | 19/80 failures: 10/40 streamed echo, 9/40 prompt logprobs; sweep completed |
| PR HEAD, V1 async, no reset | 0/24 failures in each of two fresh server runs |
| PR HEAD, V1 async, active-request reset, run 1 | 3 failures among 8 recorded requests; server exited before the intended 80-request sweep completed |
| PR HEAD, V1 async, active-request reset, run 2 | 2 failures among 8 recorded requests; server exited again |
| PR HEAD, V1 sync, active-request reset | 0/80 failures |
| PR HEAD, V2 async, active-request reset | 0/80 failures |

On HEAD, run 1 hit streamed failures at target reset delays of 4 and 6 ms, then the prompt-logprob request failed at 6 ms. Run 2 hit both failures at 6 ms. Measured offsets immediately before issuing the 6 ms resets were approximately 6.5–6.6 ms. Every recorded reset returned HTTP 200 with `{"success":true}`.

For the same synthetic prompt at the 6 ms position, the paired baseline returned HTTP 200 with `prompt_logprobs: [null]` for 113 prompt tokens. HEAD returned HTTP 500. For successful requests with a matching no-reset reference, response text and returned logprob values matched exactly (maximum absolute logprob difference 0).

### Reproduction

Save the script in the collapsed section below as `repro_http.py`. Run this on a dedicated localhost test server. Set `MODEL_DIR` to the local snapshot of the model revision above and `PYTHONPATH` to the runtime source checkout being tested.

Server command for V1 async:

```bash
export MODEL_DIR=/path/to/Qwen3-0.6B
export PYTHONPATH=/path/to/vllm-source
export VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
export VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model "$MODEL_DIR" \
  --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 \
  --async-scheduling
```

After `/v1/models` is ready, run the no-reset control followed by the timing sweep:

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python repro_http.py \
  --label full_head_v1_async_no_reset \
  --reset-mode none --delays 0:24:2 \
  --seed 61490 --pause 0.2 --repeats 1 \
  --output full_head_v1_async_no_reset.jsonl

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python repro_http.py \
  --label full_head_v1_async_reset \
  --reset-mode running --delays 0:80:2 \
  --seed 61490 --pause 0.2 --repeats 1 \
  --output full_head_v1_async_reset.jsonl
```

`0:80:2` tests 0, 2, ..., 78 ms, with one streamed and one non-streamed request at each delay. Requests use `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=16`, and seeded synthetic prompts of roughly 113–114 tokens:

- Non-streamed: `prompt_logprobs=1`; checks entry count against `usage.prompt_tokens`.
- Streamed: `stream=true`, `echo=true`, `logprobs=5`, `stream_options={"include_usage":true}`; checks SSE errors, `[DONE]`, array alignment, and score count against `usage.total_tokens`.
- Reset: `POST /reset_prefix_cache?reset_running_requests=true`, issued concurrently with the request after the selected delay.

For the controls, restart the server with `--no-async-scheduling` for V1 sync, or with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and `--async-scheduling` for V2 async. Run the same active-reset client command with separate labels/output files. The two HEAD async repetitions each started a fresh server and ran the no-reset control first.

### Key exception stacks

Excerpts from the complete HEAD run; paths are shortened and line numbers retained.

Streamed echo: initial HTTP 200, followed by this SSE error:

```json
{"error":{"message":"220","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}
```

```text
Error in completion stream generator.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py", line 383, in completion_stream_generator
    logprobs = self._create_completion_logprobs(
  File "vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py", line 697, in _create_completion_logprobs
    step_token = step_top_logprobs[token_id]
KeyError: 220
```

Non-streamed prompt logprobs: HTTP 500, with this output-handler failure:

```text
AsyncLLM output_handler failed.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py", line 864, in output_handler
    processed_outputs = output_processor.process_outputs(
  File "vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py", line 785, in process_outputs
    req_state.logprobs_processor.update_from_output(engine_core_output)
  File "vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 364, in update_from_output
    self._update_prompt_logprobs(output.new_prompt_logprobs_tensors)
  File "vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 149, in _update_prompt_logprobs
    else convert_ids_list_to_tokens(
  File "vllm/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py", line 165, in convert_ids_list_to_tokens
    return [tokenizer.decode([tid]) or "" for tid in token_ids]
  File "vllm/tokenizers/hf.py", line 85, in decode
    return tok.decode(*args, **kwargs)
  File "transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py", line 2896, in decode
    return self._decode(
  File "transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py", line 1136, in _decode
    text = self._tokenizer.decode(token_ids, skip_special_tokens=skip_special_tokens)
OverflowError: number too small to fit in target type
```

The server subsequently logged shutdown, and the next client request failed with `httpx.ConnectError: All connection attempts failed`. Both HEAD runs showed the same two exception types.

I hope this additional GPU evidence helps narrow down the V1 async resume path; the script below is the unchanged independent reproducer used for these runs.

<details>
<summary>Complete reproducer: repro_http.py</summary>

```python
"""Independent HTTP timing sweep for vLLM issue #61490.

Exit 1: response correctness failure. Exit 2: unusable baseline/reset.
This script resets active requests; use a dedicated reproduction server.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import hashlib
import json
import random
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

WORDS = "river stone lamp window garden quiet north copper winter paper signal forest harbor".split()


def parse_delays(value):
    if ":" in value:
        return list(range(*map(int, value.split(":"))))
    return list(map(int, value.split(",")))


async def request_completion(client, model, prompt, streamed):
    body = dict(model=model, prompt=prompt, max_tokens=16, temperature=0)
    result = {"kind": "stream_echo" if streamed else "prompt_logprobs"}
    if not streamed:
        body["prompt_logprobs"] = 1
        response = await client.post("/v1/completions", json=body)
        payload = response.json()
        result.update(http_status=response.status_code, response=payload)
        if "error" in payload:
            result["failure"] = str(payload["error"])
        elif response.status_code != 200:
            result["failure"] = f"HTTP {response.status_code}"
        else:
            scores = payload["choices"][0].get("prompt_logprobs")
            count = len(scores or [])
            expected = payload["usage"]["prompt_tokens"]
            result.update(prompt_tokens=expected, prompt_logprob_entries=count)
            if count != expected:
                result["failure"] = f"{count} prompt logprob entries for {expected} prompt tokens"
        return result
    body.update(stream=True, echo=True, logprobs=5, stream_options={"include_usage": True})
    events = []
    done = False
    token_count = 0
    async with client.stream("POST", "/v1/completions", json=body) as response:
        result["http_status"] = response.status_code
        if response.status_code != 200:
            result["failure"] = f"HTTP {response.status_code}: {(await response.aread()).decode()}"
            return result
        async for line in response.aiter_lines():
            if not line.startswith("data:"):
                continue
            data = line[5:].strip()
            if data == "[DONE]":
                done = True
                continue
            payload = json.loads(data)
            events.append(payload)
            if "error" in payload:
                result["failure"] = str(payload["error"])
            for choice in payload.get("choices", []):
                scores = choice.get("logprobs")
                if scores:
                    lengths = [len(scores.get(key) or []) for key in
                               ("tokens", "token_logprobs", "top_logprobs", "text_offset")]
                    if len(set(lengths)) != 1:
                        result["failure"] = f"unaligned logprobs arrays: {lengths}"
                    token_count += lengths[0]
            if payload.get("usage"):
                result["usage"] = payload["usage"]
    result.update(done=done, returned_logprob_tokens=token_count, events=events)
    if not done:
        result.setdefault("failure", "stream ended without [DONE]")
    if result.get("usage") and token_count != result["usage"]["total_tokens"]:
        result.setdefault("failure", f"echo returned {token_count} token scores for {result['usage']['total_tokens']} tokens")
    return result


async def main(args):
    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    results = []
    output_path = Path(args.output)
    with output_path.open("w") as output:
        def record(item):
            output.write(json.dumps(item, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            output.flush()

        async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=args.base_url, timeout=120, trust_env=False) as client:
            models = await client.get("/v1/models")
            models.raise_for_status()
            model = models.json()["data"][0]["id"]
            record({"config": vars(args), "model": model})

            def prompt(index):
                return f"nonce {index} {rng.randrange(10**9)} " + " ".join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(100))

            for streamed in (True, False):
                warmup = await request_completion(client, model, prompt(-1), streamed)
                record(dict(warmup, warmup=True))
                if "failure" in warmup:
                    print("INVALID_BASELINE", warmup["failure"], flush=True)
                    return 2
            for repeat in range(args.repeats):
                for delay in parse_delays(args.delays):
                    for streamed in (True, False):
                        text = prompt(len(results))
                        start = time.perf_counter()
                        task = asyncio.create_task(request_completion(client, model, text, streamed))
                        reset = None
                        if args.reset_mode != "none":
                            await asyncio.sleep(delay / 1000)
                            actual_offset = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
                            response = await client.post("/reset_prefix_cache", params={
                                "reset_running_requests": str(args.reset_mode == "running").lower()
                            })
                            reset = {"http_status": response.status_code,
                                     "body": response.text, "offset_ms": actual_offset}
                        result = await task
                        result.update(label=args.label, repeat=repeat, delay_ms=delay,
                                      reset=reset, prompt=text,
                                      prompt_sha256=hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest())
                        record(result)
                        results.append(result)
                        detail = result.get("failure", "OK")
                        print(f"{args.label} reset={delay:2d}ms {result['kind']:16s} {detail}", flush=True)
                        if reset is not None and reset["http_status"] != 200:
                            print("INVALID_RESET", reset, flush=True)
                            return 2
                        await asyncio.sleep(args.pause)
        summary = {"label": args.label, "requests": len(results),
                   "failures": sum("failure" in item for item in results)}
        for kind in ("stream_echo", "prompt_logprobs"):
            subset = [item for item in results if item["kind"] == kind]
            summary[kind] = {"requests": len(subset), "failures": sum("failure" in item for item in subset)}
        record({"summary": summary})
        print("SUMMARY", json.dumps(summary), flush=True)
        return int(summary["failures"] > 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8000")
    parser.add_argument("--label", default="v1_async")
    parser.add_argument("--reset-mode", choices=["running", "idle", "none"], default="running")
    parser.add_argument("--delays", default="0:80:2")
    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--pause", type=float, default=0.2)
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=61490)
    parser.add_argument("--output", default="results.jsonl")
    raise SystemExit(asyncio.run(main(parser.parse_args())))

```

</details>

Thanks again for the careful GPU matrix, it pinned the exact failure shape. I found the root cause behind both crashes and pushed a follow-up commit to this branch.

Root cause: on the redo path the resumed prefill still honors prefix-cache hits. The prompt-logprobs CPU tensor is freshly allocated with torch.empty (one row per prompt position) and only rows the resumed prefill actually covers get written. A request preempted by the reset re-hits its own just-freed blocks on the very next schedule, so the hit rows stayed uninitialized: garbage int32 ids then crashed the decode in `_update_prompt_logprobs` (your OverflowError, and the server exit), and positions that were never recomputed produced maps without their target token, which the completion-side formatter indexed without a guard (your KeyError: 220). V1 sync and V2 async were clean because the former has no drop-stale-output race and the latter re-registers on its own new-request path.

Two changes on top of the previous head:

- The scheduler now discards a prefix hit for a request that is redoing dropped prompt logprobs, so the resumed prefill recomputes the whole prompt and every tensor row is written. This mirrors the existing prefix-replay zeroing a few lines above. New regression test forces a partial hit on the resume lookup and asserts the full prompt gets scheduled; without the change it schedules only the suffix.
- The completion logprobs formatter now treats a missing sampled-token entry the same way the chat path already does (placeholder instead of KeyError), with a unit test.

Verified locally on CPU: the new scheduler and serving tests pass (red without the fix, green with it), the surrounding scheduler and completion suites are green, and my earlier source-level probes for both crash classes confirm the fixed behavior. I do not have a GPU here, so the V1 async + active-reset matrix is not rerun on my side. If you are willing to rerun your sweep against the new head, that would be the strongest check; the failure shape you measured (KeyError at 4-6 ms resets, OverflowError on the prompt-logprobs request) should both be gone, and successful requests should still match the no-reset reference exactly.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

files.patch:
@@ -881,6 +881,32 @@ def test_completion_logprobs_honors_requested_count(
     assert len(logprobs.top_logprobs[0]) == expected
 
 
+def test_completion_logprobs_missing_sampled_token_falls_back():
+    """A step map that lacks the sampled token id must not raise KeyError.
+
+    The chat path already treats a missing entry like a missing step, but the
+    completion path indexed `step_top_logprobs[token_id]` directly, so an
+    incomplete map (e.g. a recomputed prompt-logprobs pass, #61490) crashed
+    the request instead of serving the placeholder.
+    """
+    tokenizer = MagicMock()
+    tokenizer.decode = lambda token_id: f"tok{token_id}"
+    step_logprobs = {
+        11: Logprob(logprob=-0.2, decoded_token="b"),
+    }
+
+    logprobs = _minimal_serving_completion()._create_completion_logprobs(
+        token_ids=[10],  # sampled token absent from the step map
+        top_logprobs=[step_logprobs],
+        num_output_top_logprobs=1,
+        tokenizer=tokenizer,
+    )
+
+    assert logprobs.tokens == ["tok10"]
+    assert logprobs.token_logprobs == [None]
+    assert logprobs.top_logprobs == [None]
+
+
 def test_logprobs_below_minus_one_rejected():
     """Values more negative than -1 stay invalid."""
     with pytest.raises(Exception, match="must be a positive value or -1"):

@@ -1666,7 +1666,152 @@ def test_preemption_processes_stale_aux_output():
     scheduler.aux_output_connector.take_output.assert_called_once_with(request, None)
 
 
-def test_prefix_cache_stats_not_recorded_when_caching_disabled():
+def test_reset_prefix_cache_redoes_dropped_prompt_logprobs():
+    """reset_prefix_cache drops the in-flight prefill output; when that output
+    carried the completed prompt logprobs, the resumed request must carry the
+    redo directive so the runner re-registers the requirement (#61490)."""
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        enable_prefix_caching=True, async_scheduling=True, use_v2_model_runner=False
+    )
+    request = create_requests(num_requests=1, prompt_logprobs=5)[0]
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+
+    scheduler_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert request.status == RequestStatus.RUNNING
+
+    # The reset lands while the prefill step is in flight.
+    scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)
+    assert request.drop_stale_output
+    assert request.num_stale_output_tokens > 0
+
+    # The in-flight output comes back with the completed prompt logprobs and
+    # is dropped as stale: the loss must be recorded on the request.
+    scheduler.update_from_output(

The streamed echo request still raises `KeyError: 220`. The non-streamed `prompt_logprobs` request returns HTTP 500 with `OverflowError: number too small to fit in target type`; the API server then exits, interrupting the sweep.

### Environment and build scope

- Single NVIDIA RTX 4090 D, 24 GB; driver `595.71.05`.
- Python `3.12.3`; PyTorch `2.13.0` with CUDA runtime `13.0`; Triton `3.7.1`; Transformers `5.19.0`; httpx `0.28.1`.
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, loaded from a local snapshot.
- Runtime: complete PR HEAD Python source, with native/vendor build artifacts and generated version metadata from the official vLLM `0.30.0` wheel. PyTorch matches the PR's CUDA requirements. All 2,662 tracked runtime Python files were checked against the HEAD source archive and were unchanged.
- Paired runtime baseline: HEAD with only the four production-file changes reversed using `patch --reverse --fuzz=0`, corresponding to merge base `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`. It used the same dependencies and precompiled artifacts.

For successful requests with a matching no-reset reference, response text and returned logprob values matched exactly (maximum absolute logprob difference 0).

Thanks again for the careful GPU matrix, it pinned the exact failure shape. I found the root cause behind both crashes and pushed a follow-up commit to this branch.

Root cause: on the redo path the resumed prefill still honors prefix-cache hits. The prompt-logprobs CPU tensor is freshly allocated with torch.empty (one row per prompt position) and only rows the resumed prefill actually covers get written. A request preempted by the reset re-hits its own just-freed blocks on the very next schedule, so the hit rows stayed uninitialized: garbage int32 ids then crashed the decode in `_update_prompt_logprobs` (your OverflowError, and the server exit), and positions that were never recomputed produced maps without their target token, which the completion-side formatter indexed without a guard (your KeyError: 220). V1 sync and V2 async were clean because the former has no drop-stale-output race and the latter re-registers on its own new-request path.

Two changes on top of the previous head:

- The scheduler now discards a prefix hit for a request that is redoing dropped prompt logprobs, so the resumed prefill recomputes the whole prompt and every tensor row is written. This mirrors the existing prefix-replay zeroing a few lines above. New regression test forces a partial hit on the resume lookup and asserts the full prompt gets scheduled; without the change it schedules only the suffix.
- The completion logprobs formatter now treats a missing sampled-token entry the same way the chat path already does (placeholder instead of KeyError), with a unit test.

Verified locally on CPU: the new scheduler and serving tests pass (red without the fix, green with it), the surrounding scheduler and completion suites are green, and my earlier source-level probes for both crash classes confirm the fixed behavior. I do not have a GPU here, so the V1 async + active-reset matrix is not rerun on my side. If you are willing to rerun your sweep against the new head, that would be the strongest check; the failure shape you measured (KeyError at 4-6 ms resets, OverflowError on the prompt-logprobs request) should both be gone, and successful requests should still match the no-reset reference exactly.
